hints: Look backwards from the final product, what functional groups in X could be oxidised by hot KMnO4 to give two acids plus a ketone?
Count the oxygens, the product has a central C=O with no OH, so X must contain a secondary alcohol at that carbon and primary alcohols at both ends.
Think how to turn the C=C in the starting diol into that alcohol pattern without oxidising, what reagent simply adds water across a double bond?
walkthrough:
**Work backwards from the product**

Look at oxobutanedioic acid, $\text{HO}_2\text{C-CO-CH}_2\text{-CO}_2\text{H}$. It has 4 carbons like the starting material, so no carbon skeleton is lost.

It contains two $\text{-CO}_2\text{H}$ groups and one ketone $\text{C=O}$.

**Deduce what X must be**

Hot, acidified $\text{KMnO}_4$ is very vigorous. It oxidises primary alcohols to carboxylic acids and secondary alcohols to ketones.

$$\text{R-CH}_2\text{OH} \rightarrow \text{R-CO}_2\text{H}$$
$$\text{R}_2\text{CH(OH)} \rightarrow \text{R}_2\text{C=O}$$

**Match X to that oxidation**

To get $\text{HO}_2\text{C-CO-CH}_2\text{-CO}_2\text{H}$, X must be $\text{HOCH}_2\text{-CH(OH)-CH}_2\text{-CH}_2\text{OH}$. The two end $\text{-CH}_2\text{OH}$ groups become acids, the middle $\text{CH(OH)}$ becomes the ketone.

This is butane-1,2,4-triol.

**Find step 1 to make that triol**

Starting material is $\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH=CHCH}_2\text{OH}$, an alkene diol. Adding $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ across the $\text{C=C}$ gives exactly that triol.

Alkene hydration uses steam and concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$:
$$\text{CH=CH + H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{CH(OH)-CH}_2$$

options.A: Cold, acidified KMnO4 does syn dihydroxylation of C=C to give two more OH groups, so you would get a tetrol HOCH2CH(OH)CH(OH)CH2OH, not the triol shown. The X shown is also the wrong triol isomer (1,3,4-triol) and its strong oxidation would not give the 2-oxo diacid.
options.B: Hot, acidified K2Cr2O7 oxidises the two primary alcohols to acids but leaves the C=C intact, giving HO2CCH=CHCO2H. Hot KMnO4 in step 2 would then cleave that C=C, breaking the 4-carbon chain, so you could not get HO2CCOCH2CO2H which keeps all 4 carbons.
options.C: Steam with concentrated H2SO4 hydrates the C=C to give HOCH2CH(OH)CH2CH2OH. Hot KMnO4 then oxidises both primary alcohols to CO2H and the secondary alcohol to C=O, giving exactly HO2CCOCH2CO2H with the carbon skeleton intact.
options.D: Warm, acidified K2Cr2O7 oxidises primary alcohols only to aldehydes, it does not hydrate C=C. The X shown OHCCH(OH)CH2CHO already contains a secondary alcohol that cannot come from this reagent alone, and its further oxidation would give acids at both ends but keep an aldehyde-derived pattern, not the required keto-diacid.
